# Reflected-pair residual credit and a quantitative asymmetric-middle regime

This note extends the actual residual argument, not the density-allocation
menus. It gives a finite pair-family bound at one prescribed lattice anchor,
and a new ordinary-depth stability consequence of the audited symmetric-
middle three-fiber theorem. A separate exact example shows why the generic
ordinary Grünbaum bound alone does not complete this certificate globally.

## 1. A pair residual function and its sharp elementary Lipschitz bound

For (d\ge1) and (0<a\le b), define for (h\ge0)

\[
R_{a,b}(h)=\left[a-\left(2h^{1/d}-b^{1/d}\right)_+^d\right]_+,
\qquad v=2^{-d}(a^{1/d}+b^{1/d})^d.
\tag{1}
\]

It is constant (a) up to (h=b/2^d), vanishes for (h\ge v), and
is decreasing between these points. On the open intermediate interval,

\[
|R_{a,b}'(h)|
=2\left(2-(b/h)^{1/d}\right)^{d-1}
\le \kappa_d(a,b):=
2\left(\frac{2a^{1/d}}{a^{1/d}+b^{1/d}}\right)^{d-1}\le2.
\tag{2}
\]

For (d=1), (1) is piecewise linear and the intermediate slope is
exactly (-2\); no endpoint (0^0\) is used. For (d>1), (2) follows
by differentiating on its positive branch and observing (h\le v\le b\).
Continuity at both branch endpoints proves the global Lipschitz bound.

## 2. One actual anchor with several disjoint reflected pairs

Let (n,d\ge1\), let (S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\), and
let its fiber (K=C_p\) at (p\in\mathbb Z^n\) have positive (d)-volume

\(k\).

Choose any finite family of distinct unordered reflected pairs
\(\{p-z_j,p+z_j\}\), (z_j\ne0\), each with positive-volume fibers.
Let their two volumes, sorted separately for each pair, be (a_j\le b_j\).
The pairs and the central fiber are disjoint. Other fibers may remain
unassigned and their nonnegative mass is not counted in the bound below.

For (y\in K\), let \(\delta=\operatorname{depth}_{\rm raw,K}(y)\)
be its ordinary unnormalized halfspace depth. Then the single actual point
\(Y=(p,y)\) has raw mixed depth at least

\[
\boxed{\delta+\sum_j R_{a_j,b_j}(k-\delta).}
\tag{3}
\]

To prove it, take an arbitrary through-(Y\) ambient halfspace with nonzero
continuous normal. Let its middle captured volume be (q\ge\delta\), and
write (h=k-q\). For each pair, the two closed residuals have midpoint
inside the SAME missed middle half, by actual convexity and the opposite
integer displacements. If total pair capture (P<a_j\), both residuals
have positive volume, and Brunn–Minkowski gives

\[
(a_j-U)^{1/d}+(b_j-V)^{1/d}\le2h^{1/d},\qquad U+V=P.
\]

Concavity in the allocation puts its minimum at (U=P,V=0\), since
\(a_j\le b_j\). Thus

\((a_j-P)^{1/d}+b_j^{1/d}\le2h^{1/d}\),

which implies (P\ge R_{a_j,b_j}(h)\). The same bound is automatic for
\(P\ge a_j\), including empty residuals. Hyperplanes are null for all
these full-dimensional fibers, so closed complementary cuts give the exact
volume identities. Since (1) decreases, (h\le k-\delta\) proves (3)
after summing the disjoint pairs.

A pure integer halfspace through (Y\) captures the whole middle fiber
and at least one fiber from every pair, hence at least (k+\sum a_j\).
This also dominates (3). Parallel shrinking handles all merely containing
closed halfspaces. The presence of the full-dimensional middle fiber gives

\(q=\dim_H S=d\),

so these are the original intrinsic (\mathcal H_d\) masses. No boundary
mass or additional full-dimensional fiber is subtracted from the target.

## 3. Stability when the middle has depth close to one half

For exactly three positive fibers (A,K,B\) at (-1,0,1\), write their
volumes (a\le b\), (k\), and let (M=a+k+b\). Put

\[
\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d,\quad
\rho_d=((d-1)/(d+1))^d,\quad
\beta_d=\frac{\Gamma_d}{1+2\Gamma_d+\rho_d}.
\]

Assume there is an actual point (y\in K\) of ordinary raw depth

\[
\delta\ge(1/2-\epsilon)k,\qquad \epsilon\ge0.
\tag{4}
\]

There is NO symmetry hypothesis on any body. Every ordinary depth is at
most (k/2\), by complementary through-point halfspaces. By (2)–(3),

\[
\delta+R_{a,b}(k-\delta)
\ge k/2+R_{a,b}(k/2)-[1+\kappa_d(a,b)]\epsilon k.
\tag{5}
\]

The exact scalar theorem proved in
`candidate b13e43ee6ee1d8af`
states, for all these numerical volumes, that

\[
\max\{\Gamma_d b,\ k/2+R_{a,b}(k/2)\}\ge\beta_d M.
\]

Its scalar statement does not assume the existence of a symmetric body.
The larger endpoint centroid is an actual point with raw mixed depth at
least (\Gamma_d b\). Combining it with (Y=(0,y)\) and (5) proves the
deterministic two-point bound

\[
\max\{D_S(0,y),D_S(1,g_B)\}
\ge\beta_dM-[1+\kappa_d(a,b)]\epsilon k
\ge(\beta_d-3\epsilon)M.
\tag{6}
\]

For every (d\ge3\), the strict binomial inequality
\(2\Gamma_d+\rho_d<1\) gives (\beta_d>\Gamma_d/2\). In particular
the OC constant for this three-fiber class follows whenever

\[
\epsilon\le\frac{\beta_d-\Gamma_d/2}{3}.
\tag{7}
\]

At (d=3\), \(\beta_3=3/14\), \(\Gamma_3=27/64\), so the explicit
allowance in (7) is \(\epsilon\le1/896\). Thus ordinary middle depth
at least \(447k/896\) suffices, without symmetry. Formula (6) retains
the stronger actual volume-dependent factor (1+\kappa_d(a,b)\).

A point maximizing ordinary depth exists: through-point cap volume is
jointly continuous in the point and unit normal, since hyperplanes have
zero body volume. Minimizing over the compact unit sphere gives a continuous
depth function, which attains its maximum on the compact body. Thus (4)
may be posed using this attained ordinary maximum, with one deterministic
maximizer selected. This does not assert that every body satisfies (4).

## 4. An exact obstruction to replacing (4) by ordinary Grünbaum alone

Take (d=2,n=1\) and a centroided triangle (T\) of area one. Let

\[
A=T/10,\qquad K=B=T.
\]

These are actual compatible full fibers, since \((A+B)/2=(11/20)T\subset T\).
Their total mass is (201/100\). The maximum ordinary depth of a triangle
of area (v\) is exactly (4v/9\): the centroid has this lower bound, and
at any point one barycentric coordinate is at least (1/3\), yielding a
parallel vertex cap of area at most (4v/9\).

At the middle fiber, the best value available from (3), even optimizing
the ordinary source, is exactly (4/9\). Indeed (k-\delta\ge5/9\), and

\[
R_{1/100,1}(5/9)=0
\]

because \(2\sqrt5/3-1>1/3>1/10\). At either endpoint there is no nontrivial
reflected pair in the three-base set, so (3) supplies only its own ordinary
depth. Hence the maximum of this residual-star certificate over EVERY
anchor and own point is (4/9\), below the actual OC target

\[
\frac29\frac{201}{100}=\frac{67}{150}
\]

by (1/450\).

The actual middle centroid is nevertheless safe. For a centered triangle,
\(-T\subset2T\), since each negative vertex is the sum of the other two.
Thus \(-A\subset B\). Its reflected endpoint pair supplies at least
\(|A|=1/100\) in every through-middle halfspace, and the own triangle
supplies (4/9\). The resulting actual raw bound exceeds the OC target
by (7/900\).

The example isolates the limitation of the scalar residual-star bound; it
is not a counterexample to OC, to an actual centroid selector, or to a
certificate retaining reflected-subset geometry in addition to (3).
